title: Armalyte
build: Thalamus disk release, two G64 side images (a verified dump, marked (!)) from the C64 Preservation Project's 10th Anniversary Collection on the Internet Archive; sha256 of each side in orientation.md

records.c: The front end's character set, 256 characters in multicolour, copied to $7800 for the title ($B770). The scoreboard also draws its glyphs from the first two pages. Characters 0-31: the panel's digits 0-9, the super-weapon letters A, B and C (10-12, with D, E and F after them), the battery glyphs (16 none, 17 empty, 18 charged), the generator's rebuild box filling up (19-26) and the generator counts (27-31).

Characters 32-63: the weapon-level bars the scoreboard draws from this page ($20-$28), the title alphabet's punctuation (' $29, the Commodore key's sign $2A, / $2B, . $2C, , $2D, : $2E, ; $2F, ? $30, ! $31, - $32, ( $33, ) $34), the copyright sign ($35) and the digits 0-9 ($36-$3F).
Characters 64-95: the letters A-Z ($40-$59) and the first characters of the logo ($5A-$5F).
Characters 96-127: the middle of the logo's characters.
Characters 128-159: the last logo characters ($80-$8F), then the starfield icons ($90-$9B) and the player-mode icons ($9C-$9F).
Characters 160-191: the rest of the player-mode icons ($A0-$A2) and the first pictures of the ship enhancements ($A3 on).
Characters 192-223: more pictures of the ship enhancements.

Characters 224-255: the last enhancement pictures (to $E4), the lower characters of the one-player-and-drone icon ($E5-$E7), characters $E8-$FD that neither the title's texts, icons nor logo use, and $FE/$FF, solid, the title's space.

The title's texts, strings ending with $FF in the game's alphabet (A = $40, 0 = $36, space $FE), 41 of them, found through $9484/$94AD. String 0 is 41 spaces. Strings 1-6 are the high-score rows ($9029 on, 24 bytes each): place, score ("05000000" down to "00100000" at the start) and a three-letter name (DAN, RJL, JHK, an M and a W with a mark between, CYB, SYS), rewritten by high_score_check.
The sixth high-score row's score digits, where high_score_check compares and writes from.

Strings 7-18: "HIGH  SCORES", "CREDITS:", then the credits in pairs: "PROGRAMMING AND GAME DESIGN" Dan Phillips; "SYSTEM PROGRAMMING AND GAME DESIGN" John Kemp; "GRAPHICS, LEVEL AND GAME DESIGN" Robin Levy; "MUSIC  AND  SOUND  FX" Martin Walker; "PRODUCED BY:" Paul Cooper and John Harries, which no page shows.

Strings 19-30: the three-line rows of the ship-enhancement pages, each a picture of three by three characters ($A3-$E4) beside its name: munitions pod and forward fire, tail gun and vertical fire, trident and converge, generator and battery.

Strings 31-40: "KEYBOARD CONTROLS", then each key and what it does: RUN/STOP pause, SPACE remote tracking on/off, the key shown as character $2A (the code reads the Commodore key) and '?' ($30) to change each player's super weapon, Q quit (in pause), F1 one or two players, F3 starfield, F7 demo mode; and "SHIP ENHANCEMENTS".
Low bytes of the 41 title strings' addresses; the high bytes follow at $94AD.
High bytes of the 41 title strings' addresses.
Unused: zeros after the string table.

Runs once after each level file has unpacked, as the last step of the load (the unpacker jumps here). It moves the unpacked level down from $0801-$7701 to $0200-$6FFF, a page at a time with self-modified operands, then with the I/O area banked out ($01 = $34) copies $7701-$7E00 to the RAM under the I/O chips at $D000-$D6FF (the level's character set) and $7E01-$8000 to $9700-$98FF (the level's script and tables), and jumps through the vector at $B02A ($B3CC after a level load). The engine keeps this routine at $DA80 and copies it here before every load ($B7F8).

Jump table of the scoreboard and player-collision module: $9900 panel_init, $9903 panel_update, $9906 p1_collect_pod, $9909 p2_collect_pod, $990C players_start_positions, $990F panel_sprites_setup, $9912 players_hit_scenery, $9915 drone_follow, $9918 drone_colour_cycle.
Entry 2 of the scoreboard module's jump table: JMP panel_update ($99FA).
Entry 3: JMP p1_collect_pod ($9A94).
Entry 4: JMP p2_collect_pod ($9B92).
Entry 5: JMP players_start_positions ($9D0F).
Entry 6: JMP panel_sprites_setup ($9D6C).
Entry 7: JMP players_hit_scenery ($9E05).
Entry 8: JMP drone_follow ($9E78).
Entry 9: JMP drone_colour_cycle ($9F0E).

Starts the scoreboard: fills every cached value of what the panel shows ($99B7-$99BE lives and score digits, $99F2-$99F9 the battery slots, $9A2B-$9A2C, $9A5C-$9A5D, $9A8E-$9A8F, $9F70-$9F71) with $FF so that nothing matches, then calls panel_update 26 times so every item is drawn.
Offsets of the scoreboard glyphs in the font at $8800: entry n is n*8, the first byte of glyph n (32 entries). Indexed by a digit or a status value to pick the 8 rows panel_draw_glyph copies.
Glyph offsets 10-15, entered here with a super-weapon choice (0-2) to give its letter.
Glyph offsets 16-18, entered here with a battery slot's value: none, empty, charged (2 and above).
Glyph offsets 19-26, entered here with a generator's rebuild count (0-7).
Glyph offsets 27-31, entered here with a generator count (0-4).
Low bytes of where each of the eight score and lives glyphs goes in the panel sprites at $46xx (the high byte is $46). Read by the score part of panel_update with the digit's index.

Part of panel_update. Compares the eight bytes from $B005 (lives, then the six score digits $B007-$B00C and $B00C) with the copy at $99B7; at the first that differs it stores the new value, chooses its glyph (a digit, or glyph 15 for anything over 15) and draws it into the panel sprite at $46xx. When all match it goes on to the energy display ($9A35).

Copies the 8 rows of a scoreboard glyph from the font into sprite data: the source ($8800 + glyph offset, self-modified at $99A9/$99AA) is read a byte at a time and stored every third byte from the target (self-modified at $99AC/$99AD), the layout of one sprite column. $99B3 holds how many rows to copy (8, or 5 for the small glyphs).
Low byte of the glyph's place in the font, the operand of LDA $8800,Y at $99A8, patched by each part of panel_update.
High byte of the glyph's place: $88, or $89 for the weapon-level glyphs.
STA into the panel sprite through the patched operand at $99AC/$99AD; X steps by three, one sprite row per glyph row.
Low byte of where the glyph goes in the panel sprites, patched with the item's place.
High byte of where the glyph goes: $45, $46 or $47.

How many rows panel_draw_glyph copies, the operand of CPY # at $99B2: 8 for digits, letters and the generator's rebuild glyphs (set at $99A1), 5 for the small status glyphs of batteries, generator counts and weapon levels ($99EC, $9A88, $9F6A).
What the scoreboard shows for lives and the six score digits, compared with $B005-$B00C so that only a changed glyph is redrawn.

Part of panel_update. Compares the battery slots $B010-$B017 with the copy at $99F2 and redraws the first that changed (glyph from the table at $995C: values 0-2, larger ones shown as 2) at the slot's place from $9A2D, 5 rows high. When all match it moves on to the score ($9974).
What the scoreboard shows in the eight battery slots, compared with $B010-$B017.

The scoreboard's per-frame update, called by the main loop. Each call redraws at most one changed item, so the panel costs little in any frame: first the two generator rebuild counts ($60/$61, 0-7, glyphs from $995F, at $45D3 and $4713), then the batteries, the score and lives, the super-weapon letters, the generator counts and the weapon level, each part handing on to the next when it has nothing to redraw.

Where the two generator rebuild counts are drawn: low bytes $D3, $13 and high bytes $45, $47 (player 1 at $45D3, player 2 at $4713). The six bytes after it ($9A2D) are the low bytes of the battery slots in the panel sprites.
High bytes of the two generator rebuild glyphs' places, $45 and $47.
What the scoreboard shows as each player's generator rebuild count ($60, $61).
Player 2's byte of panel_cache_rebuild.
Low bytes of the eight battery slots' places in the panel sprites (player 1's four, then player 2's), with high byte $46.

Part of panel_update. Compares the two super-weapon choices $49/$4A (0-2) with the copy at $9A5C and redraws the one that changed (glyph 10, 11 or 12 from $9956) at $4621 or $46E3. When both match it goes on to the generators ($9A60).
What the scoreboard shows of the two super-weapon choices $49 and $4A; the two bytes after it are the low bytes of their places ($21, $E3).
Player 2's byte of panel_cache_super.
Low bytes of the super-weapon letters' places, $21 for player 1 and $E3 for player 2 (high byte $46).

Part of panel_update. Compares the two generator counts $B018/$B019 with the copy at $9A8E and redraws the one that changed (glyph from $9967) at $45C1 or $4701, 5 rows high. When both match it goes on to the converge display ($9F38).
What the scoreboard shows as the two generator counts; the four bytes after it are the places' high bytes ($45, $47) and low bytes ($C1, $01).
Player 2's byte of panel_cache_generators.
High bytes of the generator counts' places, $45 and $47.
Low bytes of the generator counts' places, $C1 and $01.

Player 1 against the pods and enemy shots, run by the main loop on one frame in four (when $68 is 1, taking turns with player 2's check) while player 1 is in play ($B00D >= 2). Builds a box around the ship ($B4 its x halved, $B5/$B6 its y - 10 and y + 16) and looks through the 16 objects for one in state 3 or more inside it (x within 11 of the ship). An object in state 7 or more is an enemy: player 1 is hit ($B00D = 1) unless invulnerable ($B00D = 3). Anything below 7 is a pod: it is cleared and its type in $FF30 decides. Types 1-4 add an enhancement when there is room (1 forward fire, $4B up to 3; 2 tail gun $4D; 3 $4F; 4 $47) and only sound $0E. Every other case also makes the ship invulnerable ($B00D = 3, timer $56 = $FF): a full enhancement of types 1-4, type 5 (converge: with the tail gun and forward fire 3 it raises forward fire to 5 and sets $B2; at more than 3 it puts it back to 3), type 6 ($B018 up to 4), type 7 (a 1 in the first empty one of the four slots $B010-$B013), and type 0, a pod that has not been shot. With no object in reach it checks the four enemy shots ($9C97).

The same as p1_collect_pod for the second ship ($B00E, coordinates $03/$0B/$05, enhancements $4C/$4E/$50/$48, batteries $B014-$B017, generators $B019, invulnerability timer $57). A drone ($B00E = 4) collects nothing and is never hit by an object: it goes straight to the shot test, where it only absorbs shots.

Tests the four enemy shots (state $FD60 >= 3, y $E8, x $FD10/$FD4C) against player 1's box, 6 pixels either side; a shot inside is turned to its burst (state 2) and player 1, if in normal play ($B00D = 2), is hit ($B00D = 1).
The same shot test for the second ship. A drone absorbs the shot (its state 4 is never changed), which is how it shields the player.

Puts both ships at their starting places and resets their movement: x $54 for both, y $74 and $A4, the map columns and rows they stand on ($2E/$2F, $30/$31), colours ($06-$09), and the eight movement counters $3C-$43 at 2. When the second ship is the drone ($B00E = 4) it gets the drone's colours, its lives counter $B006 is cleared and the drone's target offset ($83/$84) is set beside the ship.

Run in the interrupt at the bottom of the screen: lays the eight hardware sprites out as the scoreboard, a row at x $55, $6D, $87, $9F, $B7, $CF, $E7 and $FF (24 pixels apart but for 26 between the second and third) at y 0 (shown in the opened lower border), all grey ($0C), with pointers $16-$1D (data at $4580-$477F) in both screens' pointer slots ($73F8 and $77F8).

Kills a ship that touches the scenery: for each ship in normal play reads the two characters of the map under its nose (through the row-address tables at $85A0/$85B9 for the screen being shown and $85D2, at the ship's row and column) and marks it hit ($B00D or $B00E = 1) when either is a solid character, $21-$F5. Characters below $21 are space; $F6-$FF are the ones the ships pass through.

Moves the drone in one-player mode ($B00E = 4) while it is attached ($74 = 0): the joystick's last direction ($78, a single direction) picks an offset from the tables at $9EF8 (columns) and $9F03 (rows), so the drone sits on the side away from the way the ship last moved; the target ($83, $84) is the ship's place plus that offset, kept on the screen, and the drone steps one character toward it whenever its own movement counters ($38-$3B) are idle.
Offsets of the drone from the ship for each joystick direction: 11 column offsets at $9EF8 and 11 row offsets at $9F03, indexed by the stick's four direction bits.
The drone's row offsets from the ship, 11 entries by stick direction.

Makes the drone's colour pulse: while it is attached ($74 = 0), on the frames when the fine scroll $18 is 0 or 4, every fourth frame while the map scrolls; while detached, every second frame ($68). Steps $75 through 0-7 and sets the drone's colour $07 to $0F + $75.

Last part of panel_update. For each player adds up forward fire ($4B) - 1, converge ($B2) and tail fire ($4D), compares it with the copy at $9F70 and redraws the one that changed with a glyph from the $8900 half of the font at its place from $9F72/$9F74, 5 rows high.
What the scoreboard shows as each player's weapon level; then the places' high bytes ($45, $47) and low bytes ($DA, $18).
Player 2's byte of panel_cache_converge.
High bytes of the two weapon-level places, $45 and $47.
Low bytes of the two weapon-level places, $DA and $18.
Unused: zeros to the end of the scoreboard module's page.

The engine's first instruction, reached from the loader once the main file is in, and again after every game over and every quit (through the vector at $66). Sets the vector at $B000 to the level start ($A031), the processor port to $36, the keyboard and joystick ports' directions, CIA 2's port A to output for the video bank, sets level 1 as the next ($B002 = 0) and the next load as a new game's ($B004 = 1), and jumps to the front end ($B030), which loads level 1 again when another level is in memory.

Starts or restarts a level: stack at $0112, screen off, the play interrupt and every play variable set up (level_setup_vars), the stack page filled with $FF (the protection check at $AFAE looks for it), the 20 object y positions at 50, then the first scroll set-up ($E000), and once the raster is at line 0 the interrupts go on and the main loop starts.

The play interrupt: saves A in $0E, X in $0D and Y in $0C, acknowledges the raster interrupt and jumps through its own operand at $A06B, which points at the frame handler ($A07C) or at the next slot of the sprite multiplexer ($A319).
Low byte of the play interrupt's JMP target: frame_irq ($A07C) or the multiplexer's next slot.
High byte of the play interrupt's JMP target ($A0 or $A3).
Sets the next raster interrupt a few lines on (A holds how many lines short of the next sprite the raster is, as a negative number) and falls into the common exit.
Restores A from $0E, X from $0D and Y from $0C and returns from the interrupt. Its RTI ($A07B) is also where the NMI vector points in play, so RESTORE does nothing.

The two interrupts of each frame that are not the multiplexer's, told apart by $0F. At line $FA ($0F = 1): opens the lower border (row-24 mode until line $FC), puts the scoreboard sprites up and, unless paused ($51), runs the frame's movement: players and their fire ($AB53, $ABD9), drone colour, scrolling ($E00F, unless the level has stopped), the ships' scenery test, the enemy shots and the pause key. At line 0 ($0F = 0): shows the screen the scroll has drawn ($24 into $D018), sets the fine scroll, and starts the multiplexer for the frame ($A305).

records.s: $68 flips every frame: the main loop runs paths and waves when it is 0, animation and the pod checks when it is 1.

records.c: The multiplexer has placed every object for this frame: point the interrupt back at frame_irq and ask for line $FA.

The main loop, once per frame: waits for the multiplexer to start ($1D), plays the sound effects ($FA2C, not in the demo), updates the scoreboard, and unless paused ($51) runs the rest of the game: the level's attack waves ($AE62), the end-of-level check, enemy hits ($A54C), enemy movement and firing, enemy shots, the level script ($A93E, at the end of each scroll step), ships' fire against the scenery, the end-boss logic, explosions, the second player or drone, and drawing the map's next column into the hidden screen ($E009/$E003) or its end-of-scroll equivalent ($E00C).

records.s: Every second frame: enemies_follow_paths and waves_spawn when $68 is 0; otherwise objects_animate and one ship's pod check, each ship's every fourth frame ($76).

records.c: Sets everything up for a level: the play interrupt and NMI vectors, the interrupt jump at frame_irq, CIA interrupts off, zero page $02-$FF cleared, the super-weapon choices from $B020/$B021, the quit vector $66 = $A000, $01 = $35, video bank 1 ($DD00 = 2, screens at $7000/$7400, characters at $7800), colour RAM to 8, the object tables at $FD00-$FFF7 cleared, the second module's tables ($E048 screen rows, $E03F paths, $E042 sprite rows, $E045 sprite columns), sounds off and tune 1 set up (it only plays in the demo), then a DEC of both invulnerability timers $56/$57, meant to turn the cleared zeros into 255 frames; but music_init has just left its track pointer there ($CD67), so ship 1 starts invulnerable for 102 frames (about 2 seconds, measured) and ship 2 for 204. Then the flash and explosion steps, sprites off, forward fire at two shots ($4B, $4C = 1), both ships at their start, 360 scroll phases run to fill the screen with the map, the scroll at its start ($21 = 0, or $7F on level 7), the level's character set copied from under the I/O area ($D000-$D6FF) to $7900-$7FFF, the scoreboard, and the starting enemies ($AB0F).

Starts the sprite multiplexer for a frame: the list of up to 20 objects sorted by y ($EC-$FF, built by the main loop) is walked from $12 = $13 down, hardware sprites 2 to 7 used in turn; each slot's interrupt ($A319) waits for the sprite it reuses to have been drawn (its y + $16 against the raster), then sets its x, y, pointer in both screens, x high bit and colour from the object's tables. When the raster is not yet there it sets the next interrupt for that line and leaves. Objects in state 0 or 1 are skipped.

Tests the enemies against the players' fire on the screen: every object below 16 in state 5 or more with hit points in $FEE0, or in the boss stage ($6F) only objects $86 down to 0 (the boss's guards and its core). Reads the screen characters at the enemy's place and two rows below, through the row tables $8600/$9500 and the column table $9600; a fire character ($F6 or higher) there is a hit. The fire character is cleared (unless it is a super weapon's, $FB or higher, which goes on hitting), and in the boss stage the hit goes to boss_part_hit. Otherwise the enemy loses a hit point (sound $1D); at zero an enemy (state 7 or more) explodes (state 2) and scores ($A9EF), or, with a group number in $FFD0, takes its whole group with it for 5,000 points (group_destroyed). A pod (state 5 or 6) shot instead changes to the next enhancement ($A5F4).
High byte of the row-table read in enemies_hit_by_fire (LDA $8600,Y): $86 or $87 by the screen being drawn, from $A5F2.
The fine-scroll phase halved, patched into the SBC # at $A589 so the enemy's column allows for the scroll; the rest of enemies_hit_by_fire follows.
The points a kill scores, in hundreds: the operand of LDA # at $A5D6 before JSR score_add_hundreds, patched by the level script from kill_points_by_speed.
High bytes $86 and $87 of the two screen-row tables, chosen by the screen being drawn ($17); written into the operands at $A578 and $A8F3.

A shot pod changes shape: its type in $FF30 goes to the next of the seven enhancements, and its frame, colour and the hits it takes before changing again come from the tables at $A64C, $A65C and $A654 (five fewer hits with two players, $B00E != 4). Sound $0F. After 7 the type goes to 0, an unshot pod's, while the frame, colour and hits are forward fire's (Y = 1, $A5FE-$A603): until its next change the pod looks like forward fire and, collected, gives only an unshot pod's invulnerability.
Every live object of group A ($FFD0) explodes (state 2), and the group scores 5,000 points (5 thousands, through $A9FE) in place of the kill's own points.

The pod's sprite frame for each enhancement 1-7 (index 0 unused): $23 $24 $25 $28 $29 $26 $27. Then at $A654 the hits each needs before it changes again (11, 11, 11, 11, 17, 17, 32) and at $A65C its colour (12, 12, 12, 14, 10, 12, 12).
The hits a pod needs before it changes again, by its type 1-7: 11, 11, 11, 11, 17, 17, 32 (five fewer in a two-player game).

Lets an enemy fire when one of the shots allowed this stage ($6B + 1 of the four) is free: picks an enemy in state 7+ whose fire flag ($FF80) is set and whose firing mode ($FF94 bits 0-1) allows it now (mode 2 fires at once; the others when level with the target), checks that no live shot is within 45 lines of the new one, and starts a shot (state 2 into $FDB0) at the enemy's place aimed at the target chosen by $A79E: it sets the shot's x and y directions ($FD88/$FD9C) and, with the speed $6A, works out how many steps on the long axis to one on the short ($FD74/$FF68).

Picks which ship the enemies aim at: player 1, or the second ship when it is the only one in play or on alternate shots ($7A); its y goes to $7B, its x halved to $7C, and $7D (3 for player 1, 4 for the second ship) is kept with the shot in $FDC4. Also takes the stage's sound numbers from the tables at $A83D/$A7DA by the fine-scroll phase ($18).
Sound numbers chosen by the fine-scroll phase $18 ($A79E puts them in $7F); $A83D, after the code, is the other set, for $80.

Clears every enemy shot that has gone past the top ($35) or bottom ($E6) of the play area. In the boss stage ($6F) it then watches the boss's guards: while the scroll is stopped, once objects 1 to $86 are all gone $86 is cleared, and from then on the core can be hurt (boss_part_hit). It plays the boss's sound $1E whenever no other sound is playing, and ends with the parts' hit flash ($AD5D).
The second set of shot sounds, for $80, by fine-scroll phase.

Runs down each object's delay ($FDA0, objects 0-19) once a main-loop pass: an object with no state that still has a delay counts down, and at 1 it comes to life in the state kept for it in $FDB4, with its place in its path ($C4) and its delays cleared. Objects 16-19 are the four enemy shots, and their follow byte ($FFBC) is the enemy that fired: unless $AD or $6F is set, a shot whose delay reaches 1 is born only if that enemy is in state 5 or more, with the stage's shot sound ($7F) on voice 1; otherwise its delay drops to 0 and the shot is cancelled. Also counts the live enemies (objects 0-15) less one into $B4, and with more than 12 live outside the boss stage bars one shot for each enemy over 12, from shot 0 up: a shot in flight is turned to its burst ($FD60 = 2), an unused one has its delay cleared ($FDB0 = 0), and $FFB8 marks it barred from firing (enemies_fire).
A JMP $A856 that no path reaches, between two parts of objects_timers.

Part of objects_timers for an object with no state: a delay of 0 leaves it unborn, 1 brings it to life in its kept state (an enemy shot only while the enemy that fired it is alive, or else it is cancelled), and more counts down by one each pass.

Ends every enemy shot (state 3 or more) that runs into the scenery: reads the two screen characters at the shot's place through the row tables ($8600/$8700 by the screen being drawn, $9500) and the column table $9600, and a solid character ($21-$F5) turns the shot into its burst (state 2, moving down: $FD9C = 1), with sound $1F outside the boss stage.
High byte of the row-table read in shots_hit_scenery: $86 or $87, from $A5F2.

Runs the level's script once a scroll step, when the fine scroll $18 is at 7, every eight frames; it goes on doing so while the scroll is stopped ($52), because the stopped redraw ($E36B) steps $18 too. While stopped it counts the stop down instead, $54 from 5 to 0 and then $53 by one, so each unit of $53 is 48 frames, about a second. When $53 reaches 0 everything explodes as if the boss's core had gone (level_end, $AC20). Otherwise it compares the scroll position ($21, $20) with the next event's in the level's tables at $9700/$9748 (event $55; events 0-10, the script stopping at 11). An event sets the enemy speed $6A from $9760 (a speed below 3 has the number of games completed, $B02D, added, to at most 3), the points a kill scores ($A5D7, from the speed and the player count), the boss to start ($6D, from $9754), the number of enemy shots allowed ($6B, from $976C, events 0-9), and by its flags at $973C: bit 0 the background colours from $970C/$9718/$9724, bit 1 a stop of the scroll for $9730 units of 48 frames (0 counts as 256).
Stops or restarts the scroll: turns over the stop flag $52 and moves the map's ring position $1B (0-$29) back one column as the scroll stops, or on one column as it restarts.

The points an enemy is worth, in hundreds, by enemy speed $6A (0-7): 1, 3, 3, 4, 5, 5, 5, 5; then at $A9E6 what the player count adds (index $B00E: 3 for two players, 0 with the drone). The level script patches the sum into the LDA # at $A5D6, so a kill scores 100 to 500 points, 300 more in a two-player game.
What the player count adds to a kill's points, by $B00E: 3, 3, 3, 3 for a second player, 0 for the drone.
Tail of score_add_hundreds: keeps the hundreds digit when it did not carry.

Adds A hundred points to the score, which both players share: six decimal digits $B007 (ten millions) to $B00C (hundreds), one digit to a byte; the panel shows them with two fixed zeros after. A carry out of the ten-thousands digit ($B00A) also gives an extra life ($AEC4), so one comes every 100,000 points; at the top the score wraps to zero. Entry $A9FE adds A thousands, $AA0D ten thousands, $AA2E millions.
score_add_millions: adds A millions to the score, from the millions digit $B008 up, carrying into the ten millions; level_complete adds the million for a level here.

Keeps the attack waves apart: walks the y-sorted object list and for each enemy moving vertically ($FD78 sign) looks for another live object close above or below it in its path (within $28 or $25 lines, after skipping $B7 = 5 entries); one that has not yet appeared is removed, and otherwise the enemy reverses both directions ($FD8C, $FD78), dies into its burst state 2 and plays sound $1F.

The play screen's video chip settings: every sprite multicolour, fine scroll 7 with 38 columns, screen at $7400 and characters at $7800, raster interrupt at line 0 enabled, no expansion or priority, black border, white background, sprite colours 1 and $0B, character colours $0E and 6.

Reads the keyboard's bottom row once per frame (only changes count, against $72): RUN/STOP asks for a pause ($77 = 1); Q quits to the front end, but only while paused; the Commodore key moves player 1's super weapon on ($49, through $ABD6) and SPACE, with the drone, detaches or recalls it ($74). Then the '/' key (the '?' key) moves player 2's super weapon on ($4A). Each change of weapon plays the weapon's sound from $ABD3.
The sound of each super weapon, 0-2 ($0A, $0B, $0D), then at $ABD6 the next weapon after each (0 to 1, 1 to 2, 2 to 0).
The next super weapon after each: 0 to 1, 1 to 2, 2 to 0.

Reads both joysticks into $78 (port 2, player 1) and $79 (port 1, player 2). In the demo ($B01A) both ships are out of play, the music plays (tune 1, which every level start sets up), and when it ends the demo quits to the front end.

Part of enemies_hit_by_fire in the boss stage: a hit on boss object X (0-3) plays sound $1E and counts down the part's hit counter $8B; each time that reaches 0 the part's reserve $87 goes down by one, and when the reserve is spent the part is destroyed (so a part takes $8B hits, plus 256 for each unit of $87). Object 0, the core, takes no hits while its guards are alive ($86). The core's end ends the boss through level_end ($AC20: everything explodes; 50,000 points for a mid-level boss, the end sequence for the boss at the end of the scroll); any other part explodes (state 2), with its whole group when it has one.

Ends the level or the boss: every live object explodes, the shot count goes back to what it was before the boss (the LDA # at $AC36, patched by boss_start) and sound 1 plays; if the scroll has reached its end ($21 = 0) the end sequence starts ($AD = $94, both ships invulnerable), otherwise 5 ten-thousands of points are scored ($69 = 5 tells the main loop the mid-level boss is gone).
The shot count restored when a boss or level ends, the operand of LDA # at $AC36: 2, or what boss_start stored there; the rest of level_end follows.

Starts a boss when the level script asks ($6D = 1 the boss at the end of the level, from the table at $9778; 2 the mid-level boss, from $97D8) and none is running ($6E): sets $6E and $6F, keeps the shot count for later, clears the 16 objects and fills them from the level's table: the number of guards ($86, objects 1 on that must go before the core can be hit), shots allowed ($6B), the spawn settings ($97/$98), the hits and 256-hit reserves of the core and guards ($87-$92), each object's state, x, y and movement ($FDB4, $FD00, $D8, $FDC8) and 20 bytes of spawn positions and types ($99-$AC).
Where each boss's table is, by $6D: low bytes $00, $78, $D8 and high bytes $00, $97, $97 (none, $9778, $97D8).
High bytes of the boss tables, by $6D: $00, $97, $97.

Makes a boss part flash white when it is hit: for each of the four parts compares its hit counter ($8B) with the copy at $8F; on a change it keeps the part's colour in $93 and sets white ($FD14 = 1), and the next frame without a change puts the colour back.

Lets the boss release enemies: when its core object is alive, with spawning on ($98 not $FF) and every spawn slot free, it puts a set of enemies from the boss table's spawn list ($99-$AC: x, y, x high bit, state, movement) into objects 15 down, one at a time or ($98 negative) all at once, with a delay of 5 before each appears; $97 counts down the sets.
The last spawn slot boss_spawn fills, the operand of CPY # at $ADFE: $97 less one to release one enemy at a time, or $FF for a whole set.

The end sequence has finished: scores 1 million, gives an extra life to each player in play, keeps the super-weapon choices for the next level ($B020/$B021), and unless a lives counter has gone negative moves to the next level ($B002 + 1; after the eighth it also counts a completed game in $B02D, which makes the next round faster) and forces it to load ($B003 = $FF), screen off and sound off; then back to the front end ($B030), which loads it.

Plays the end of a level once the end boss is gone: $AD counts down from $94; at $62 the boss bursts ($AEEC); below that the background colours step down through the table at $AEA4 (the three indexes $AE/$AF/$B0 fall one by one) and at 1 the level is complete ($AE25).
The colour steps of the end-of-level fade, read by level_end_sequence at three indexes that fall toward 0.
Gives each player in play one more life (at most 15; never the drone) and plays sound $0C.

The end boss breaks up: the four enemy-shot objects (16-19) are placed at object 0's place, the core, with colour $0A and four fixed diagonal speeds, to come to life after a delay of 2 in state 2, the burst state. objects_animate then replaces the frame $BF set here with the burst frames $2E-$37 at once, so four explosions fly apart and are removed after $37. Sounds 1, 0 and 3 on voices 1, 2 and 3.
Turns the pause on or off when RUN/STOP was pressed ($77), at the end of a scroll step ($18 = 0) or when already paused, and resets the ships' colours.
Each frame: while paused, fire on either joystick ends the pause; in the demo, fire quits to the front end through the vector at $66. Otherwise checks for RUN/STOP (pause_toggle).
Makes every live object (0-19) explode (state 2) and clears every delay; used when the scroll reaches the end ($21 = $FA).

Protection: the stack page was filled with $FF at the level start; if any of $0138-$013F is anything else (something has used the stack far below the game's own, as a cartridge's freeze would) it wipes $B000-$FFFF with the I/O banked out and jumps to the KERNAL's reset at $FCE2.
The page being wiped, the high byte of STA $B000,Y at $AFC3, counted up until it wraps past $FF.
A copy of the front end's timing check ($BDC8) that no code calls: with $B02C clear, CIA 1's timer B must read between 0 and $7F, or the game is wiped ($AFBB).
The address of the level start ($A031), set by engine_start; the loader returns through it.
High byte of level_start_vector.
The level being played, 0-7 for levels 1-8 and 8 for the ending: the index into the file-name table at $B3EA.
The level now in memory; when it differs from $B002 the front end loads $B002's file. $FF forces a load.

1 while the next load is for a new game: set by engine_start (at power-on, and after every game over or quit, which go through $A000) and cleared when a level is completed (level_complete) or the ending hands back. After a load with it set the game goes to the title instead of "PRESS FIRE TO START" ($B3CC), and the loading music fades out at block 18 ($B702).
Lives of player 1 ($B005) and player 2 ($B006), 0-15; the panel shows them at either end.
Player 2's lives.
The score both players share, a decimal digit to a byte: $B007 ten millions down to $B00C hundreds (the panel adds "00").
The score's millions digit.
The score's hundred-thousands digit.
The score's ten-thousands digit; a carry out of it gives an extra life.
The score's thousands digit.
The score's hundreds digit, the last one stored.
State of player 1 ($B00D) and the second ship ($B00E): 0 out of play, 1 hit, 2 in play, 3 invulnerable, 4 (second ship only) the drone.
State of the second ship: 0 out, 1 hit, 2 in play, 3 invulnerable, 4 the drone.

Player 1's four battery slots ($B010-$B013) and player 2's ($B014-$B017): 0 for no battery, 1 for an empty one, up to 7 for one holding six charges. The generator fills them ($EB00) and a super weapon draws on them when the generator's own charge is short ($EC87).
Player 2's four battery slots.
Player 1's ($B018) and player 2's ($B019) generator count, 0-4.
Player 2's generator count.
1 while the demo plays (and while quitting); the main loop skips the sound effects and enemy hits then.
Each player's super-weapon choice, kept from one level to the next.
Player 2's super-weapon choice, kept between levels. $B022-$B025 after it are not used.
1 for one player with the drone, 0 for two players; set on the title by F1 or the stick.
Where the mover at $9680 jumps after a load: $B3CC.
High byte of post_load_vector.
Not zero for the first timing check after a start, which skips it (the timer has not run a whole frame yet).

How many times all eight levels have been finished in this game: counted by level_complete after the eighth level, cleared whenever the title is shown ($B030). Added to an event's enemy speed below 3, to at most 3 (level_script).
Which of six colour sets the title uses (counted down at each visit).
Which of three starfields play uses (0-2), stepped by F3 on the title and read at $F72F.

The front end, entered at power-on, after a game, between levels and from the pause's quit. Stack at $0112, CIA 1's timer B latch set to $4D07 cycles (one PAL frame and a line, for the timing check at $BDC8), the post-load vector at $B02A, screen and sprites off, the stack page filled with $FF, tune 0 set up, zero page cleared ($B53E), and the level loaded if $B002 differs from $B003 ($B388, which does not come back). Otherwise sets the title interrupt and NMI ($B128, $B1BF), video bank 1, I/O in, the 24 title balls' order and the title screen ($B770); starts tune 2 and, after a game, checks the score against the high scores ($BA72, whose name entry plays to tune 2's cue); then clears the count of completed games ($B02D = 0) and starts tune 0, the title's tune; then the first title text, the player-mode text, the balls' colours for this visit (one of six sets from $B361/$B367/$B36D), and the title loop.
The title's raster interrupt: saves the registers and jumps through its own operand at $B134 to the ball multiplexer's next slot ($B165) or to the frame part ($B1C0).
Low byte of the title interrupt's JMP target.
High byte of the title interrupt's JMP target.
Starts the frame's ball multiplexer: one fewer sprite on, $0B and $04 = 7 (the next hardware sprite), every sprite's y to 0, and the interrupt pointed at the multiplexer ($B165).

Places the title's balls (up to 24, sorted by y in the order at $80) on the eight hardware sprites in turn: waits until the sprite it reuses has been drawn, then sets its x ($FD18), y ($98) and frame ($FD00, into the pointer at $77F8). When the raster is not there yet it sets the next interrupt for that line and leaves. After the last ball it sets the frame part for line $F9.
RTI: the front end's NMI does nothing, so RESTORE is ignored.

The title's frame interrupt, alternating with title_balls_start by $02: sprites off, the next interrupt at line $16, then the timing check ($BDC8), the stack check ($B838), the music ($C059), the ball count ($B270), the balls' movement ($B1ED) and the start keys and stick ($B58A).

Moves the title's balls: each has an x and a y step index ($FD48, $FD60) into the curve at $8500 and a direction ($FD30, $FD78); the step is added or taken off the position and the index walks up to $77 and back to 0, turning the direction at each end, so the balls swing along a smooth curve. Then sorts them by y ($B29B).
Every ten frames brings one more ball out, up to 24.
The 24 sprite frames of a ball's spin ($C0-$C7 and back), stepped by $B373.
One pass of a bubble sort of the ball order at $80 by y ($98), so the multiplexer meets them top to bottom.

The title's main loop, once a frame: waits for the frame interrupt ($0B), draws the colour bars of the logo ($BCD8), sets the background and character colours at lines $5A, $6B and $7A (the text's colours from $B2EF/$B2F4/$B2F9, set by the fade), runs the title text pages ($B85B), every tenth frame steps the balls' spin ($B373), and sets the colours for the bottom line at $DD.
The title text's background colour, the operand of LDA # at $B2EE in title_loop, set by the fade.
The title text's first character colour, the operand of LDA # at $B2F3, set by the fade.
The title text's second character colour, the operand of LDA # at $B2F8, set by the fade; the rest of title_loop follows.
Puts all 24 balls at the start of their curve: x $80, y $AF, step indexes $40 and $1E, frame $BF, spin step $0B, and alternating directions in groups ($07, the colour set's length).
The six colour sets of the title balls, one per visit: at $B361 how many balls share a direction, at $B367 the sprite multicolour, at $B36D the sprites' colour.
The sprite multicolour of each of the title's six colour sets.
The sprite colour of each of the title's six colour sets.
Steps each ball to its next frame from $B283.

Loads level $B002 when it is not the one in memory ($B003): stack reset, the loading screen built ($B7F8), $0200-$03FF cleared, music 3, the loading picture ($B6A4), the KERNAL's interrupt vectors at $0314/$0318 pointed at an RTI ($B522), and the file named by the letter at $B3EA/$B3F3 opened on drive 8 through the KERNAL (SETLFS at $FFBA, with the ROM in) before the fast loader takes over ($B3FC). The load ends at the level's mover ($9680), which comes back at $B3CC.

Where every load ends ($B02A). With $B004 set (a new game's load: at power-on, or after a game over beyond level 1) it goes to the front end and the title. Otherwise it takes two batteries and two generators away ($B723 twice, which also makes both ships invulnerable at the start), shows "PRESS FIRE TO START" on the loading screen, waits for fire, stops the music and waits for it to end, and starts the level, or for $B002 = 8 runs the ending at $0801.

The one-letter file names on side B, by $B002: D E L H U N A R for levels 1-8 and M for the ending. Then at $B3EA the low and at $B3F3 the high bytes of each letter's address, the file name pointer given to the KERNAL.
Low bytes of where each level file's one-letter name is, for the KERNAL's SETNAM.
High bytes of where each level file's name is.

Cyberdyne's fast loader. Opens the file through the KERNAL's serial routines (TALK, TKSA, ACPTR at $ED09/$EDC7/$EE13 in the ROM, which is in while it runs; the RAM under them is game code); a status with bit 1 set means the file is not on the disk ($B5CC). Then sends the drive code from $8600 in 32-byte M-W blocks to the drive's $0700 and starts it with M-E $07AB, builds the bit-pair decoding table at $8700 ($BCA1), sets the loading interrupt ($B6E4), and receives the file two bits at a time through CIA 2's port A ($B4E1): two header bytes, then the data stored from $0801 upward, with the loading screen's block counter counting down after each block ($BDE5), until a short last block, and jumps to the unpacker at $0812.
Sends LISTEN, SECOND $6F and "M-" to the drive (CIOUT), the start of an M-W or M-E command.

Receives one byte from the drive: signals ready on CIA 2's port A, waits for the drive's clock, avoids the raster's bad lines (lines below $31, or where the line and 6 is 2), then reads the port four times, each read giving two bits that the tables at $8700-$871F turn into their place in the byte.
Points the KERNAL's IRQ and NMI vectors ($0314, $0318) at an RTI that pulls the KERNAL's saved registers ($B538) and at title_nmi, for the time the ROM is in during a load.
Pulls Y, X and A as the KERNAL's interrupt entry saved them and returns.
Clears zero page $02-$FF.

The front end's video chip settings: sprite positions 0, 38 columns with multicolour characters, no expansion or priority, every sprite multicolour, character colours 2 and 1, sprite colour 1, background $0A, screen $7400 and characters $7800.
Clears $B005-$B01F: lives, score, player states, batteries, generators and the demo flag.

Reads the joysticks on the title: fire on either starts a game (the second ship is the drone when $B026 = 1, a second player when 0; three lives each; both ships invulnerable at the start) through the level start vector; left chooses one player with the drone, right two players.
The file was not found: shows "TURN DISK TO SIDE B PRESS FIRE" on the loading screen, waits for fire with the stack check running, and goes back to the front end to try again.
"TURN DISK TO SIDE B PRESS FIRE", in the game's own alphabet (letters from $40, space $FE).
Writes the title's three fixed lines into the screen at $7400: the copyright line, "CYBERDYNE SYSTEMS" and "PRESS FIRE TO START".
"© THALAMUS MCMLXXXVIII" ($35 is the copyright sign), then at $B646 "CYBERDYNE SYSTEMS" and at $B65E "PRESS FIRE TO START", in the game's alphabet.
"CYBERDYNE SYSTEMS", in the game's alphabet.
"PRESS FIRE TO START", in the game's alphabet.
Shows "PRESS FIRE TO START" under the loading picture, waits for fire, fades the music out and waits for it to stop, blanks the screen, and starts the level (or the ending at $0801 after level 8).

The loading screen: front-end video settings, video bank 2 ($DD00 = 1) with the screen at $8000 and characters at $8800 ($D018 = 2), "LOADING" written at $83D1 and the level's block count, two digits from $B6D2/$B6DB, at $8333.
"LOADING", then the tens ($B6D2) and units ($B6DB) of each file's block count as digits ($36 is 0): 67, 63, 67, 44, 60, 62, 48, 69, 48 for D E L H U N A R M.
The tens digit of each file's block count.
The units digit of each file's block count.
Sets the loading interrupt ($B702) at line $35 with the I/O in and the timing check skipped once, and turns the screen on.
The interrupt while a level loads: plays the music ($C059), and on the first load (the one before the title, $B004 set) starts the music's fade ($C058 = 5) when the block counter $02 reaches 18.

Run twice after loading a level: takes away the last battery found in slots 3, 2 or 1 of each player (from the third slot down: $B012, $B011, $B010, and $B016-$B014), one generator each ($B018, $B019, while there are any), and makes each player in play invulnerable for the start ($B00D/$B00E = 3; never the drone).

Builds the title: screen $7400-$77FF filled with spaces ($FE), the character set copied from $8800-$8FFF to $7800-$7FFF, colour RAM 8, then with the I/O banked out the logo's screen from $D700 to $7400, the curve table from $D800 to $8500, the sprites of the balls and logo from $DB00-$DEFF to $7000-$73FF and the colour bar table from $DA00 to $9600.

Clears the loading screen at $8000-$83FF to spaces and colour RAM to 8, then with the I/O out copies the loading picture's first page from $D700 to $8000, the drive code from $D900 to $8600 and the mover from $DA00 to $9600 (so $DA80 becomes $9680).
The front end's stack check: as $AFAE, but a failure clears $E000-$FFFF, $A000-$A0FF and $B000-$B0FF and stops the processor with a JAM ($B845).

Protection: clears $E000-$FFFF, a page at a time (the first STA's operand high byte at $B84B counts up until it wraps), and on every pass the same two pages $A000-$A0FF and $B000-$B0FF, whose operands nothing changes; then halts on the JAM at $B85A.
The page being wiped by wipe_and_halt, the high byte of its STA, counted up until it wraps.
The JAM ($02) that stops the processor at the end of wipe_and_halt; only a reset gets past it.
The title's changing text: waits out the timers $13/$14, then by $19 draws the next page's lines (0, $B8A6), fades them in (1) or out (2), or blanks them (3).
Blanks a title line: 40 spaces ($FE) stored through the STA's own operand, patched with the line's screen address from $B93B/$B931.
Low byte of the title line being blanked.
High byte of the title line being blanked; the rest of title_text follows.

Draws one line of the current title page ($1B, 0-6): the page's table (pointers at $B945/$B94C) gives the line's string number and its three fade colours, the string's address comes from the tables at $9484/$94AD, its length is found by its $FF end, and it is written centred on the screen line from $B931/$B93B. After the last line the page fades in.

The screen address of each title text line: high bytes at $B931, low bytes at $B93B. Then at $B945/$B94C the low and high bytes of the seven pages' tables, and the tables themselves: for each page its three colours and its lines' string numbers.
Low bytes of the ten title lines' screen addresses, 40 apart from $75B8.
Low bytes of the seven title pages' tables ($B953, then 13 bytes apart).
High bytes of the seven title pages' tables, all $B9.

The seven title pages, 13 bytes each: the string numbers of its ten lines (0 a blank line; the strings through $9484/$94AD), drawn centred, then three colours that become the first entries of the three fade tables. Pages 1 and 2 are the credits, 3 and 4 the ship enhancements, 5 the high scores, 6 and 7 the keyboard controls. Strings 17 and 18, "PRODUCED BY:" and "PAUL COOPER AND JOHN HARRIES", are on no page, so the title never shows them.
Steps the title text's colours up the fade tables at $B9EC/$B9FC/$BA0C, then holds the page ($13/$14 = $C8) before fading out.
Steps the colours back down; at the end of the table blanks the lines next.
The three fade tables of the title text's colours (background, and the two character colours), read at $B9C3.
The second of the title text's fade tables: the first character colour.
The third fade table: the second character colour.

Shows the high-score page with "GAME OVER" while the name is entered (by the interrupt, $BA63): points the title interrupt's frame part at $BA63, draws the page's text and loops until the music has ended ($C057 = 0), then goes back to the front end. When $C058 holds $28, fire sets it to 0 first; the $28 is stored by high_score_check itself (at $BAA9), on the way here when the score did not make the table.
The frame interrupt during name entry: name entry ($BB3C), music, logo bars, stack check.

After a game: turns the score into digits of the alphabet ($36 = 0) and clears it, then finds its place among the six high scores (rows 24 bytes apart from $9029, each row's score at $902E + 24n and its name 15 bytes after); if it qualifies, moves the lower rows down, writes the score in, points the entry routine's self-modified operands at the new row and starts name entry ($BA1C).
The high-score row compared with, the low byte of CMP $90xx,X at $BA92, patched from $BB2A.
High byte of the row read when the lower high scores move down, patched from $BB2B.
Low byte of the row written as they move down, patched from $BB2A; then the new score is written into its row and name entry is set up.
Low byte of the row the new score is written into, patched from $BB2A.

The new score as eight digits of the alphabet ($36, "0") and its name, three full stops ($2C, "..."), laid out as a high-score row from its score on; then at $BB2A the low bytes of the six rows' score places ($90A6 for the sixth up to $902E for the first), and at $BB30 and $BB36 the low and high bytes of the six rows' places in colour RAM ($DB06 for the sixth up to $DA16 for the first), which $BAF0 writes into high_score_name_entry's colour instructions at $BB42 and $BB52.
Low byte of the sixth row's score place, $A6.
Low bytes of the fifth to first rows' score places.
Low bytes of the colour-RAM places of the six rows' names, for the flashing letter.
High bytes of the colour-RAM places of the six rows' names.

Name entry, three letters: the current letter flashes ($D800 colour EOR 6); every sixth frame the stick moves it: up steps the letter on (A-Z, then space, then back), down steps it back, and fire moves to the next letter; after the third the entry ends ($C058 = 3).
Low byte of the name's colour place, the operand of LDA $D800,X at $BB42, patched from $BB30.
High byte of the name's colour place, patched from $BB36.
Low byte of the name's colour place for the STA at $BB52.
High byte of the name's colour place for the STA at $BB52; the rest of name entry follows.
Low byte of the row whose letter is read to step it up, patched from $BB2A.
Low byte of the row the stepped-up letter is written to.
Low byte of the row whose letter is read to step it down.
Low byte of the row the stepped-down letter is written to.
Writes "GAME  OVER" at $754F.
"GAME  OVER" in the game's alphabet.
Draws the player-mode icon on the title, two characters by two at $7798/$77C0 (one player with the drone, or two players by $B026), and the third option's icon by $B02F at $77BE/$77E6.
The characters of the player-mode icons ($BC2D/$BC30 two players, $BC33/$BC36 one player and drone) and of $B02F's three settings ($BC39, $BC4D, $BC51).
The two-players icon's lower row ($FE, $9E, $9F).
The one-player-and-drone icon's upper row ($A0-$A2).
The one-player-and-drone icon's lower row ($E5-$E7).
Starfield setting 1's icon, upper characters ($90, $91).
Starfield setting 1's icon, lower characters ($92, $93).
Part of title_mode_text: draws starfield setting 2's icon from $BC4D/$BC4F, two characters over two, at $77BE/$77E6 (settings 0 and 1 take theirs from $BC51 and $BC39 just before).
Starfield setting 2's icon, upper characters ($94, $95).
Starfield setting 2's icon, lower characters ($96, $97).
Starfield setting 0's icon, upper characters ($98, $99).
Starfield setting 0's icon, lower characters ($9A, $9B).

Reads the function keys on the title (keyboard row 0, changes only): F7 starts the demo ($B01A + 1, then the level start), F1 switches between one player with the drone and two players ($B026), F3 steps the starfield setting $B02F through 0, 1 and 2 (read by the star routine at $F72F); each change redraws the icons.
Builds the loader's decoding tables at $8700-$871F from the 32 bytes at $BCB8: each of four 8-byte tables turns a read of CIA 2's port (bits 6 and 7) into its two bits in place.
The bit values for the four reads of a byte ($A0 $50 $0A $05, $20 $10 $02 $01, $80 $40 $08 $04), expanded by $BCA1.

From line $31 changes the background and both character colours on every raster line under the logo, 40 lines, from the tables at $9600/$9628/$9650; the delays at $BD99-$BDB3 keep each change on its line.
Delays of a few cycles for logo_colour_bars, entered at different points of the same bytes ($BD99, $BD9A, $BD9F, $BDA9): each BIT $EA is two bytes, so entering one byte in is a NOP followed by more.
A delay for the logo's colour bars: three BIT $EA and eight NOPs, 37 cycles with the JSR and RTS (39 entered at $BD99).
Entered here, the colour-bar delay runs from the middle of a BIT: $EA is a NOP, so this is a shorter delay of the same NOPs.
A shorter colour-bar delay: BIT $24 and eight NOPs, 31 cycles with the JSR and RTS.
Waits for raster line 0 and blanks the screen ($D011 = 0).
Waits for raster line 0 and turns the screen on ($D011 = $1B).

Protection, run in every title frame: with $B02C clear, CIA 1's timer B (a one-shot started at the last check with $4D07 cycles, one PAL frame and a line) must read 0-$7F, so the checks must come one PAL frame apart to within about 60 cycles; anything else (a stopped or slowed machine, an NTSC machine's shorter frame) wipes memory and halts ($B845). Then restarts the timer.
Counts the two-digit block counter on the loading screen ($8333/$8334, digits from $36) down by one.

Starts tune A (0-3): copies its eight-byte header from $C765 + 8A to $C4E7 (the low and high bytes of each voice's track, then the two tempo bytes), silences the three voices, reads each voice's first track entry ($C43C), sets the volume to 15 (the fade level $C4B2 = $10) and turns the music on ($C057 = $FF) with no fade ($C058 = $FF).
$FF while the music plays, 0 when it has stopped or faded out.
The fade speed: $FF for none, otherwise the volume drops by one every this many frames plus one. A track can set it ($FD); the front end also sets it and waits on it as a cue.

Plays the music once a frame, when it is on. A fade lowers the volume ($C4B2 into $D418) and stops the music at zero. Then for each voice, 2 down to 0 ($C4EF its register offset): on a beat ($C4B4 = 0) counts the note down ($C50D) and at its end reads the next one from the voice's pattern (number $C504, address from $C785/$C7D2, place $C501): a byte with the length (bits 0-5), bit 6 for a rest (the gate held off) and bit 7 for an extra byte (an instrument, or with bit 7 set a slide into $C522); then the note (bits 0-6, frequency from $C555/$C5B5; bit 7 ties it to the last, without a new attack). A new instrument sets the waveform, effects, pulse and envelope from its two eight-byte entries at $C615 and $C6BD. $FF ends a pattern, which repeats ($C507) or gives way to the track's next entry ($C43C). Every frame each voice runs its effects: a pulse-width sweep between two limits, vibrato after a delay, a slide, and by the instrument's flags ($C54C) a waveform switch (1), a two-note arpeggio (2), a short note falling in pitch (4), an attack waveform ($10) or attack note ($20) for the first frames; then frequency, pulse and waveform go to the chip. Last, the beat counters step.

Reads a voice's next track entry (track from $C4E7/$C4EA, place $C4F5) through the pointer $56/$57, zero-page bytes play also uses as the two ships' invulnerability timers: a byte below $80 is a repeat count for the pattern number after it; one with bit 6 set opens a loop of the entries after it, played (bits 0-5) times, and the next such byte met inside the loop sends the reader back to its start until the count runs out; $FD sets the fade speed from the next byte; any other byte of $80 or more is stored as the pattern number, where $FF sends the voice back to the start of its track and the rest stop the music.
The volume, 15 while playing ($10, less one before use), stepped down by a fade.
Frames until the fade's next step.
The beat counter: notes move on when it is 0; it counts down from $C4ED each frame.
Counts down from $C4EE; when it runs out the beat counter is reloaded early, which lengthens the odd beat.
The register offset of the voice being played (0, 7 or 14).
The instrument given by a note's extra byte, $FF for none.
The new instrument's attack and decay.
The new instrument's sustain and release.
The pulse sweep's step, from the instrument.
The pulse sweep's upper limit (high nibble of the width).
The pulse sweep's lower limit.
A downward slide's step this frame.
The track byte being read.
Vibrato: for each of 16 kinds, the frames each way ($C4BF) and the shift that turns the gap to the next note into the step ($C4CF); then at $C4DF the eight delays before vibrato starts.
The vibrato depth: how far the gap to the next semitone is halved, by kind.
The delays before vibrato starts, picked by the high nibble of the instrument's vibrato byte: 0, 10, 16, 25, 37, 50, 62, 75 frames.
Low bytes of the three voices' tracks for the tune playing.
High bytes of the three voices' tracks.
The tempo: frames between beats, less one.
The second tempo count: every this many frames plus one the beat restarts early.
The three voices' register offsets: 0, 7, 14.
Each voice's instrument number times 8, its place in the instrument tables.
Each voice's place in its track.
Each voice's track loop flag ($FF inside a loop).
Each voice's loop count.
Each voice's loop start in its track.
Each voice's place in its pattern.
Each voice's pattern number ($FF restart the track, other values of $80 up stop).
How many more times each voice plays its pattern.
The first byte of each voice's note: length, rest and extra-byte flags.
Beats left of each voice's note.
Each voice's waveform and gate byte.
Each voice's note number (0-95).
Each voice's flag ($FF) that the instrument's attack frames are over.
Each voice's instrument number.
Each voice's gate mask: $FF, or $FE to hold the gate off.
Each voice's pulse sweep direction (0 up, 1 down).
Each voice's slide: $C0 and up slides up by the low six bits each frame, $80-$BF down.
Each voice's vibrato direction.
Frames until each voice's vibrato starts.
Each voice's vibrato depth shift, negative once set up.
Each voice's vibrato phase flag.
Each voice's vibrato frame count.
Frames each way of each voice's vibrato.
Low byte of each voice's vibrato step.
High byte of each voice's vibrato step.
Low byte of each voice's frequency.
High byte of each voice's frequency.
Each voice's note byte as read (bit 7 a tie), or the new instrument to force an attack.
Low byte of each voice's pulse width.
High byte of each voice's pulse width.
Each voice's instrument effect flags.
Frames left of each voice's attack waveform or note.
Frames since each voice's note began; bit 0 alternates the waveform and arpeggio.
Low bytes of the frequencies of 96 notes, eight octaves of semitones.
The low-byte table read one note on, for the gap to the next semitone that vibrato works from; from here it runs on to the 96th note.
High bytes of the 96 notes' frequencies.
The high-byte table read one note on, for the vibrato gap; from here it runs on to the 96th note.

The first eight bytes of each of 21 instruments: attack and decay, sustain and release, waveform, effect flags, a spare byte, pulse width high, pulse sweep step, and pulse limits (high nibble the top, low the bottom).
The instruments' sustain and release, at +1.
The instruments' waveform, at +2.
The instruments' effect flags, at +3.
The instruments' starting pulse width high byte, at +5.
The instruments' pulse sweep step, at +6 (0 for none).
The pulse sweep limits at +7 of each instrument; from here the table runs on through instruments 1-20, eight bytes each in the same order.

The second eight bytes of each instrument: the attack's length in frames, the attack note, the attack waveform, the waveform switched to, the vibrato byte (delay kind in the high nibble, vibrato kind in the low), the arpeggio note (bit 7: relative), and two spare bytes.
The instruments' attack note (bit 7: relative to the note), at +1.
The instruments' attack waveform, at +2.
The instruments' second waveform for the waveform switch, at +3.
The instruments' vibrato byte, at +4.
The arpeggio note at +5 of each instrument's second entry (bit 7: relative); from here the table runs on through instruments 1-20.

The four tunes, eight bytes each: the three voices' track addresses (low bytes, then high bytes) and the two tempo counts. Tune 0 ($CC74, $CCDD, $CD36; 1, 8), tune 1 ($CD67, $CDB4, $CE0B; 1, 1), tune 2 ($CE32, $CE95, $CF02; 1, 1), tune 3 ($CF65, $CF68, $CF79; 1, 8).
Low bytes of the 77 patterns' addresses ($C81F-$CC73).
High bytes of the 77 patterns' addresses.
The 77 patterns: notes as a length byte (bit 6 rest, bit 7 an extra instrument or slide byte), then the note (bit 7 tie), each pattern ending with $FF.
The second half of the 77 patterns, from pattern 33 (at $CA5B) to the last; same format.
The tracks of the four tunes, three voices each: repeat counts and pattern numbers, loops (bit 6), $FD and a fade speed, and $FF to start the track again.
Unused: zeros after the music.
The first 256 characters of the title and loading screens, the Armalyte logo in characters $5A-$8F with spaces ($FE), copied to $7400 for the title and to $8000 for the loading screen.
The steps of the curve the title's balls swing along, copied to $8500: title_balls_move adds or takes the entry at each ball's index (0-$77) from its x and y.

The fast loader's drive code, sent to the 1541's RAM at $0700 and started at $07AB. From the track and sector the drive's own open found ($18/$19), it follows the file's chain of sectors, reading each with its own job code at $0700 (the raw bytes from the head, decoded by the drive ROM at $F8E0 and checked), and sends each data byte to the computer two bits at a time on the serial bus's clock and data lines ($1800), four writes a byte after a handshake; the last sector sends only its used bytes, and errors go back through the ROM's job exit ($F969).

The logo's colour bars, copied to $9600 for the title: three tables of 40, one entry for each raster line of the logo ($9600 the second multicolour into $D023, $9628 the background into $D021, $9650 the first multicolour into $D022), then eight zeros.
The code of move_level_into_place, kept here and copied to $9600-$96FF with the colour bars before each load ($B7F8), where it runs at $9680.
Sixteen sprite frames, copied to $7000-$73FF for the title (frames $C0-$CF): $C0-$C7 the spinning ball, then smaller shapes and blanks.
The last four title sprite frames ($CC-$CF), copied from this page to $7300.
Unused: zeros at the top of the RAM under the I/O chips.

The second module's jump table, 25 entries: $E000 objects_sort, $E003 scroll_draw_phase, $E006 star_chars_clear, $E009 scroll_fine_step, $E00C scroll_stopped_redraw, $E00F stars_animate, $E012 enemies_follow_paths, $E015 objects_init_new, $E018 waves_spawn, $E01B objects_move, $E01E objects_window, $E021 objects_animate, $E024 ships_to_sprites, $E027 ships_move, $E02A ship1_bank, $E02D ship2_bank, $E030 ships_state_step, $E033 generators_recharge, $E036 char_shots_move, $E039 ship1_fire, $E03C ship2_fire, $E03F paths_table_build, $E042 sprite_rows_build, $E045 sprite_columns_build, $E048 screen_rows_build.
